sections.html:
Gadsden is the Etowah County seat in northeast Alabama, spread along both banks of the Coosa River with the southern tip of Lookout Mountain rising just north of the center. Birmingham is about 56 miles southwest, Huntsville about 72 miles northwest and Chattanooga about 90 miles northeast. The city covers about 38.7 square miles at 581 feet, with an estimated 33,367 residents in 2025.

Population peaked at 58,088 in 1960 and stood at 33,945 in 2020, after the steel and rubber plants closed in the 1970s and 1980s. Fewer buyers chasing a large number of houses is the main fact of this market. The 2024 survey estimates 12,746 households and 16,513 housing units, so a good number of units stand empty. Median household income is $40,345, which limits how much repair cost a buyer can absorb.

River bottom, valley floor and mountain edge all sit inside the city limits, so two houses a few miles apart can differ sharply in condition and value.

Winters average 41.3 degrees in January and summers 80.6 in July, with 60 to 61 days a year at 90 degrees or higher. About 60 nights a year drop below freezing, which puts older pipes in crawl spaces and garages at risk. Heat and humidity wear on air conditioning and roofs too.

A tired roof or an aging cooling system belongs on your condition list. Inspectors check both first, and buyers with loans often ask for repairs afterward.

Gadsden City Schools runs fourteen schools: eight elementary, three middle, one high school and two specialty schools. Gadsden City High School opened for the 2006 to 2007 school year after three older city high schools merged. The Etowah County Schools office is in Gadsden, yet that district covers only addresses outside the city limits, so be careful when a buyer asks about zoning.

Interstates 59 and 759 and U.S. Highways 411, 431 and 278 serve the city, along with a trolley system, Greyhound service and the Northeast Alabama Regional Airport. Houses near the I-59 exits are within reach of the Birmingham job market.

Etowah County's Revenue Commissioner values property, and each year moves through the same dates.

MonthTax step in Etowah County
October 1Tax due
January 1Tax delinquent
FebruaryTurned over to Probate Court
AprilAdvertised for sale
MayTax sale

After a tax sale, the owner has three years to redeem by paying the taxes, interest, fees and penalties at 12 percent a year. A home you live in is Class III, assessed at 10 percent of value.

Because a tax debt sticks to the parcel, a new owner inherits whatever an earlier owner left unpaid. For that reason the closing office looks at tax status before a signing is set.

Alabama taxes a transfer at 50 cents for each $500 of value, as Alabama Code 40-22-1 provides, and the probate office adds a fee for recording. A new owner is told to file the deed with probate first, then bring it to the Revenue Commissioner to have the property assessed.

Hold on to the closing statement and the tax receipt in case a question about the tax year arises later. Address changes must reach the county in writing. Mailed notices are a courtesy, so owners owe the tax whether or not a statement shows up.

  • Save a copy of the recorded deed and the settlement statement.
  • Check that the tax year was split correctly.
  • Write to the Revenue Commissioner with your new mailing address.

Back taxes turn up often on Gadsden houses, especially inherited ones, and they do not end a sale. A payoff figure is requested, the balance comes out of your proceeds, and the lien is cleared for the next owner.

Waiting is the bigger risk. After the bill goes to probate court in February and is advertised in April, you have fewer choices about how and when to sell. If yours is late, call the Revenue Commissioner's office and ask where it stands.

sections.h2: What a Gadsden seller can do
sections.html:
Three paths exist: list, sell it yourself, or take cash. Listing reaches the widest audience, but a buyer with a loan needs an appraisal and an inspection, and a house in rough shape may fail one or both.

  • Use an agent when the house shows well and time is on your side.
  • Go private when you have the time and can manage the paperwork.
  • Choose cash when the house needs work, carries a tax or title problem, or came from an estate.

Cash Home Buyers buys Gadsden houses as they stand, and an offer can be declined.

sections.h2: How buyers see a Gadsden house
sections.html:
Gadsden has far more houses than households, and the population has fallen for decades. That means buyers can be choosy, and a house priced for a market that no longer exists will sit. Price it to the condition it is actually in.

Houses near the river, in the valley and along the mountain edge each draw a different crowd. Say which one you are in, and what has been updated, in the first message you send a buyer.

Heirs often sell because the house is far from where they live and the upkeep adds up. Before anyone can sign a deed, the court papers must show who has authority, so a probate attorney is the first call. After that, collect the deed, the latest tax bill and any lender statement.

If taxes are behind, the balance is paid from the sale at closing. If utilities are off or the house is empty, a buyer paying cash can still look at it as it stands. Keep insurance active until the closing date so a loss does not fall on you.

sections.h2: Papers to gather before you call a buyer
sections.html:
• The recorded deed, or the trust papers if the house is held that way.
  • The newest tax bill and proof of whether it is paid.
  • A payoff statement from any lender with a lien.
  • The names of everyone on title, including heirs.
  • A list of repairs you know about, from the roof to the plumbing.

With these in hand, the title search goes faster and you can compare offers on equal terms.

Once an offer is accepted, an examiner searches the record for liens, back taxes and ownership questions, and any lender supplies a payoff figure. On closing day you sign the deed and settlement statement, the payoff is sent, and the deed is filed at the Etowah County probate office.

Bring photo ID, every key and garage opener, and papers showing who owns the house. Living in Gadsden is not a requirement; plenty of owners are elsewhere and complete the sale by mail or through a title office.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Gadsden house with unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is paid from your proceeds at closing because the tax stays with the parcel. Ask for a payoff figure.

faqs.q: When does Etowah County turn unpaid taxes over for sale?
faqs.a: Bills are due October 1 and delinquent January 1. Late accounts move to probate court in February, are advertised in April and are sold in May.

faqs.q: How much is the deed tax on a Gadsden sale?
faqs.a: The state takes 50 cents per $500 of value, and a recording fee is added.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Gadsden house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers accept the present condition, while buyers with loans often need the house to meet lender standards.

faqs.q: Do I need to live in Gadsden to sell my house here?
faqs.a: No. Out-of-town owners often finish the sale by mail or through a title office.
